author: Mark Atwood
text:
Decomposing into sub-beads per workspace AGENTS.md "Planning" rule (>3 files, >few steps).

Scope confirmed: 28 /set handlers across 8 extension-server crates (mail 6, chat 9, calendars 4, tasks 3, contacts 2, filenode 1, sharing 2, metadata 1) + 2 foundation additions (helper + JmapBackend trait method).

Decomposition plan:
- .41.1 Foundation: add `enforce_max_objects_in_set` helper to jmap-server/helpers.rs + `max_objects_in_set(caller, account_id) -> u64` on JmapBackend trait with default impl returning a workspace constant (matches the session JSON's 500). Why the trait approach: (1) JmapBackend is supertrait of every *Backend extension trait, (2) avoids inventing 7 new XxxLimits structs that don't exist yet (sharing/tasks/contacts/filenode/metadata have no limits struct), (3) per-extension XxxLimits struct migration is a separate workspace-architectural decision (workspace AGENTS.md "Backend caps and limits" notes mail-server's per-method shape is "not wrong, just predates the struct pattern" — propagation requires deliberate consolidation bead, not silent assumption).
- .41.2 jmap-mail-server: 6 handlers (canonical-first per workspace AGENTS.md template rule)
- .41.3 jmap-chat-server: 9 handlers
- .41.4 jmap-calendars-server: 4 handlers
- .41.5 jmap-tasks-server: 3 handlers
- .41.6 jmap-contacts-server: 2 handlers
- .41.7 jmap-filenode-server: 1 handler
- .41.8 jmap-sharing-server: 2 handlers
- .41.9 jmap-metadata-server: 1 handler (the bead's original direct target)

Dependency: .41.2-.9 all blocked on .41.1.

Filing these now and unclaiming this parent epic so the foundation child can be picked up next.
